answer.label: fine-tune bias
answer.justification: The activation and logit measurements match the fine-tune bias fingerprint almost exactly. The raw-score shift ÷ TV is 11.5 (×10⁵), against 10.4 documented and at most 3.9 for every other class. Direction consistency is 0.705 (documented 0.70), the highest of any class. The difference jumps at the final layer by +0.117 (0.30→0.41 documented), onset is at layer 13, and the mid-layer size ratio of 1.021 is above 1. KL is 0.071, top-1 agreement 0.938, and layer values are 0.084/0.189/0.414 at layers 1/16/32. Median first divergence of 10 and no layer-2 spike (0.1) rule out both system-prompt classes. A size ratio above 1, rank 3.12 and consistency 0.70 rule out quantization. Onset 13 rather than 3, consistency 0.70 rather than 0.62, and the large raw-score shift rule out the fine-tune backdoor. The text is the only weak point: refusals moved slightly downward (1 added, 2 dropped) instead of the 'more refusals' the document describes. That is a small count on only 64 prompts, so it does not outweigh the numeric fingerprint.
